citations.claim: pre-collision energy conserved, near initial 1790 J
first violation step 7 energy 23888 exceeds allowed 1974 (E0 1790)
heavy body spuriously gains ~51 m/s from rest on collision
light body retains high speed, momentum not conserved

counterfactual.change: Changed only bodies[0].m from 16.9435 to 1.0 (equal masses) keeping all other fields, dt, steps identical; this removes the large mass-ratio and collision impulse is computed correctly with no energy violation

explanation: Energy blow-up occurs on first inter-body collision when masses are very unequal. At step 6 bodies are separate with energy ~1790 J (conserved). At step 7 they collide (gap 0.046) and the heavy body (m=16.94, initially at rest) acquires ~51 m/s while light body retains ~45 m/s, raising total energy to ~23888 J (>12x allowed) and momentum from -47.9 to -787, indicating impulse/velocity update scales with mass incorrectly (momentum not conserved, energy created). Equalizing masses eliminates the bug, confirming mass-ratio dependent collision impulse error.
vision_note: From steps 4 to 6 two blue circular bodies approach each other with a shrinking gap, and at step 7 they make contact and slightly overlap. There is no wall or tunneling visible, just a normal first inter-body collision between two initially separate bodies.
